scores.evidence_span:
The strongest initial niche is:

> **Evidence-tested AI applications, product building, and startup economics for technical founders and hands-on product operators.**

This combines three connected needs:

- Evaluating whether AI applications genuinely work.
- Understanding how to build and operate AI-enabled products.
- Interpreting industry developments through product, technical, and commercial consequences.
scores.rationale: Explicitly prioritizes a niche combining practical AI applications, industry interpretation, and entrepreneurship.

scores.evidence_span:
Every test should state:

- Task and intended user.
- Baseline.
- Inputs and constraints.
- Model or tool version.
- Evaluation rubric.
- Results.
- Failure cases.
- Cost and time.
- Data-handling considerations.
- What the result does and does not establish.
scores.rationale: Specifies concrete evidence classes for evaluating the recommended applied-AI niche, including comparative results, version information, operational constraints, and economics.

scores.evidence_span: YouTube is the best default primary platform because the account’s core differentiation depends on demonstrations, evidence, technical explanation, and narrative depth. Long-form videos can combine screen recordings, diagrams, code, business analysis, and personal delivery.
scores.rationale: Names an option and identifies observable format capabilities supporting technical demonstrations and business analysis. The connection to industry trends and entrepreneurship is less explicit in this factual support.

scores.evidence_span:
### Ben’s Bites and The Rundown AI: newsletter aggregation

[Ben’s Bites](https://www.bensbites.com/) [10] and [The Rundown AI](https://www.therundown.ai/) [11] illustrate the market for fast, accessible AI briefings.
scores.rationale: Names two identifiable aggregation options and states their briefing format, providing a verifiable contrast-side characteristic.

scores.evidence_span: Unlike AI-news feeds, generic educators, or promotional influencers, it tests claims in real workflows, exposes failure cases and costs, connects technical choices to business consequences, and distinguishes verified evidence from firsthand experience and opinion.
scores.rationale: Directly compares the preferred operator-lab approach with news feeds on validation and decision usefulness, identifying consequential differences.

The strongest initial niche is:

> **Evidence-tested AI applications, product building, and startup economics for technical founders and hands-on product operators.**

This combines three connected needs:

- Evaluating whether AI applications genuinely work.
- Understanding how to build and operate AI-enabled products.
- Interpreting industry developments through product, technical, and commercial consequences.
scores.rationale: Selects the operator-lab niche and explains its selection through the three preference-specific needs it combines.

scores.evidence_span:
Transferable lesson: consistent filtering and concise packaging solve a genuine audience problem.

Strategic warning: aggregation is increasingly easy to reproduce with AI. A new account should not compete with established briefing products unless it has a distinctive geography, sector, proprietary dataset, or practitioner lens.
scores.rationale: Acknowledges aggregation as viable but explicitly downgrades competing with established briefing products because their aggregation function is readily reproducible.

scores.evidence_span: Publish one technical test, one build log, one business teardown, and one trend interpretation.
scores.rationale: Provides executable publication actions that collectively implement AI applications, entrepreneurship, and industry interpretation.

scores.evidence_span:
A news item qualifies only if it materially affects:

- Product capability.
- Build-versus-buy decisions.
- Costs.
- Distribution.
- Regulation.
- Customer demand.
- Competitive structure.
scores.rationale: Defines an actionable editorial qualification rule linking industry developments to applied-AI and entrepreneurial decisions rather than unrestricted news coverage.

scores.evidence_span: A new account should not compete with established briefing products unless it has a distinctive geography, sector, proprietary dataset, or practitioner lens.
scores.rationale: States conditions under which aggregation competition might be viable, but does not say when generic technology-news aggregation would become better than the recommended niche. The required reversal remains incomplete.
